title: Structure-sheaf maps and derived global sections
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let D(O_X) be its unbounded derived category [def-pc-derived-category], put A=Γ(X,O_X), and let RΓ:D(O_X)→D(A) be the unbounded right derived functor of the module-valued global-sections functor [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology, def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. Let A[0] denote the free rank-one A-module placed in degree zero and O_X[0] the degree-zero structure sheaf. There is a family of additive equivalences a_E:Hom_D(O_X)(O_X[0],E) ≃+ Hom_D(A)(A[0],RΓ(E)), natural in every E: a_E'(g≫f)=a_E(g)≫RΓ(f) for every f:E→E' and g:O_X[0]→E. There is no quasi-coherence, boundedness, quasi-compactness, or separatedness assumption.

source.place: Proposition perfect-proposition-compact-is-perfect (Tag 09M1), proof, first paragraph; structure-sheaf case

proof.text: Use functorial K-injective replacements of module-sheaf complexes. The category is Grothendieck abelian and these replacements exist by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The localization bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] computes maps from O_X[0] into the replacement J.

Evaluate an O_X-linear map at 1. In degree n this identifies Hom(O_X,J^n) with Γ(X,J^n). In degree zero the chain map equation says the section is closed; a homotopy is a degree minus one section whose differential is the difference. This gives the same cycles and boundaries as maps of complexes A[0] to Γ(X,J). A[0] is K-projective, so these homotopy classes equal derived maps from A[0] to QΓ(X,J). The right-derived-functor comparison on a K-injective complex identifies QΓ(X,J) with RΓ(QJ).

Lift a derived morphism between the K-injective representatives to a homotopy class using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Evaluation at 1 commutes with postcomposition and with global sections of a chain map. Homotopic lifts give the same maps. Comparison homotopy equivalences of resolutions intertwine this calculation, so the additive equivalences descend and satisfy the stated naturality for every derived morphism.

theorem derivedStructureSheaf_globalSections_hom (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)))
    let RΓ := (RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).rightDerivedFunctor
    let A₀ := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (ModuleCat.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤))
          ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op ⊤)))
    ∃ e : ∀ E : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))) ⟶ E) ≃+
        (A₀ ⟶ RΓ.obj E),
      ∀ (E E' : schemeDerivedCategory X) (f : E ⟶ E') (g :
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ⟶ E),
        e E' (g ≫ f) = e E g ≫ RΓ.map f
